news.snippet: * Today’s most visible AI beneficiaries are infrastructure providers, but long-t...
news.raw_snippet: * Today’s most visible AI beneficiaries are infrastructure providers, but long-term value may accrue to a broader, less obvious group of companies. * Valuation remains critical, as technological revolutions do not always reward the companies that appear to be the most obvious early beneficiaries. Investors have spent much of this year trying to understand how artificial intelligence (AI) will reshape markets and which companies are most likely to benefit over time. There seems to be no debate that AI matters, but the more interesting question is how investors should attempt to profit from it. AI is likely to be an enduring technological theme, and investors understandably want exposure to what may prove to be one of the defining economic shifts of the coming decades. However, we think there is an important distinction between the short-term winners from today’s AI investment cycle and the businesses that may ultimately capture the long-term economic value it creates.

news.raw_snippet: *Databricks has signed terms for a strategic funding round that values the company at US$188 billion, with proceeds earmarked to expand its enterprise AI portfolio, strengthen governance tools, accelerate AI-native database development, and support future acquisitions as organizations increasingly seek measurable returns from artificial intelligence investments.*. As enterprises shift their AI strategies from experimentation to measurable business outcomes, Databricks is strengthening its position in the market through a new strategic funding round. The company announced it has signed a term sheet for financing that values Databricks at US$188 billion, with the transaction expected to close later this summer. "This new capital will allow us to continue advancing our multi-model AI strategy to meet growing customer demand while strengthening Unity AI Gateway, expanding Genie and accelerating the development of Lakebase.". The company says its Data and AI Platform addresses these challenges by unifying data management and artificial intelligence within an infrastructure designed for AI agents.

news.raw_snippet: ## The Valuation Surge That Signals a New Era. When a company's valuation climbs to $188 billion—a 40% increase in just a few months—it reflects more than strong investor enthusiasm. It signals growing conviction that enterprise data infrastructure is becoming a foundational layer of the AI economy. Private investors committing billions of dollars at increasingly higher valuations are expressing confidence not only in Databricks' current business but also in its long-term strategic position within one of technology's fastest-growing markets. **Invest in top private AI companies before IPO, via a Swiss platform:**. It reflects investor confidence that Databricks can monetize one of the most critical layers of enterprise AI adoption by becoming the platform connecting data, governance, and intelligent applications. Yet AI systems are only as valuable as the data they can access, and most organizations continue to store information across disconnected business units, cloud platforms, and legacy databases.

news.title: Meta Hiring Former AWS Executive Fuels Cloud Ambitions
news.snippet: Meta Platforms (META, Financials), the technology corporation that owns Facebook...
news.raw_snippet: Meta Platforms (META, Financials), the technology corporation that owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, is bolstering its artificial intelligence leadership with the hire of long-time Amazon Web Services CEO Dave Brown. He helped launch Amazon's EC2 cloud service and most recently managed its compute and machine-learning units, Bedrock and SageMaker.The hire supports the assumption that Meta is still dedicated to extending its AI infrastructure, Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson said. There's no sign the company is pulling back on capital spending or changing its strategy because of excess data center capacity, he said.The hiring comes as major tech companies rush to construct bigger AI platforms and obtain the computational power needed for ever-more-complex models.Meta has continued to invest in AI infrastructure and sees experienced cloud executives as a vital part of its long-term strategy.Investors will look for more signs that Meta aims to extend its AI offerings beyond its consumer platforms into enterprise cloud services.

news.raw_snippet: # Chinese CEO leaves US to launch successful AI startup despite ‘many opportunities’. Chinese artificial intelligence startup Moonshot AI has temporarily suspended new subscriptions for its flagship Kimi K3 model after an overwhelming surge in demand strained its computing capacity. Founded in 2023 by Yang Zhilin, a Carnegie Mellon University graduate, Moonshot has emerged as one of China’s most closely watched AI startups. Moonshot’s rapid rise has also renewed interest in Yang’s decision to leave the United States and build his company in China. “I think there’s a lot of confusion and misinformation about Zhilin’s visa, H-1B lottery, immigration, and why he left the U.S.,” Salakhutdinov wrote in a post on X. “Zhilin had many opportunities to stay in the U.S. if he wanted to,” he wrote. However, he emphasized that Yang’s move back to China reflected a personal entrepreneurial choice rather than a lack of opportunities in the United States.

news.raw_snippet: D1g1t launches MCP servers for advisers; Smartria releases SmartArchive for communications; and Mariner partners with Humanity Lab for AI workforce. ## **D1g1t Launches MCP Servers for Advisers**. D1g1t LLC, a wealth-tech provider, launched the d1g1t MCP server, a connector built on the open model context protocol standard that links its enterprise wealth management platform directly to general-purpose artificial intelligence tools such as Anthropic’s Claude, OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Microsoft’s Copilot. The d1g1t MCP exposes the platform’s core capabilities as tools that AI agents can use on an adviser’s behalf to search, read and reason based on external data sources. Smartria LLC, a cloud-based compliance management platform for registered investment advisers, broker/dealers and compliance consultants, launched SmartArchive, an artificial-intelligence-powered digital communications archiving and surveillance capability that gives firms a single platform to capture, monitor and review business communications across channels. The partnership marks the largest AI workforce partnership within a registered investment adviser and positions Mariner as the first wealth management firm to adopt the model at enterprise scale.
